new_statements.rule_in_words: Provisional analysis by the only linguist to have worked on the language: Vidunda is a pitch-accent (not fully tonal) language in which, by default, the penultimate syllable of a noun carries the high pitch/accent; a minority of nouns have the high elsewhere (e.g. antepenultimate isadásada, i-bóngoya) and these lexical exceptions are written with an acute. The author explicitly marks the analysis as preliminary ('so far it seems', tone 'not properly covered for the time being').
new_statements.exceptions: Yes: nouns whose high pitch is not on the penult are lexical exceptions, marked with an acute in the authors' orthography (isadásada p.118; i-bóngoya in Legère 2009:222).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about nouns in citation form (plant names elicited as isolated words); nothing on verbs, phrases, or interaction with phrase-final position. Framed as high tone/pitch accent rather than 'stress'.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes Chividunda as spoken in the core mountain villages Vidunda, Chon'hwe and Udunghu (Vidunda Ward, Kilosa District) = Glottolog vidu1238 / ISO vid; no dialect differentiation reported. Statement is restricted to nouns (plant-name citation forms).
